name: Vertical: A Spire Drama
description: A premium neural-feed drama set entirely within the upper forty floors of the Spire, following the interlocking corporate intrigue of three families across two competing corponation dynasties and the neutral-space mediators who profit from their conflicts. The show is technically independent but is widely understood to be financed by a Vantablack shell company, and its unfailingly sympathetic portrayal of Tier 5 characters has been dissected extensively by media critics who note that every act of cruelty is narratively redeemed and every structural injustice is personalized into a family tragedy. The neural immersion includes bespoke sensory packages — the weight of tailored chrome, the particular silence of soundproofed altitude — that have been described as 'aspirational pharmacology.'
cultural_impact: Vertical has become the primary cultural reference point for Tier 3 aspirational fantasy, and behavioral economists have noted a measurable correlation between subscription rates and decreased participation in tier-rights advocacy groups in the same demographic cohort.
story_hooks: A runner crew hired to deliver physical media to a Vertical production location discovers the package contains unencrypted casting notes that describe real Spire residents by name as character inspirations — residents who have recently died under ambiguous circumstances.
A Tier 2 actor hired as a neural-feed body double for a Tier 5 character retains fragmented sensory memories of things they weren't supposed to experience during recording sessions.
The show's most popular character — a morally complex corponation mediator — is revealed to be based on a real person who never consented, and that person is still alive and very unhappy.
